subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: Find the real values of x and y if (x − 1)/(3 + i) + (y − 1)/(3 − i) = i.

mark_split.label: Combine the two fractions over (3 + i)(3 − i) = 10
Expand the numerator into real and imaginary parts
Compare parts to get two equations

recall_prompt: Say how you would find x and y — how you combine the fractions, what you compare, and how you solve the two equations.
insider_note: The two denominators are conjugates, so one multiplication gives the real common denominator 10 — rationalising each fraction separately doubles the work for the same marks. The right side becomes 10i, whose real part is 0: those two comparisons are where the third mark sits.

steps.label: Combine the fractions
steps.margin_note: First mark. The two denominators are conjugates, so their product (3 + i)(3 − i) = 9 + 1 = 10 is real — that is the common denominator, and it is a plain number.

recall.must_convey: That the two fractions are combined over the common denominator (3 + i)(3 − i) = 10.
accept: combine the fractions over three plus i times three minus i which is ten
the common denominator is ten because the two denominators are conjugates
cross multiply, the bottom becomes nine plus one equals ten
rendu fractions ni common denominator ten meeda kalapali
put both over three plus i into three minus i, that is ten

steps.why: Because 3 + i and 3 − i are conjugates, their product is real. Combining over it removes every i from the denominator in one move — no separate rationalising is needed.
common_mistakes: Pairing (x − 1) with (3 + i) instead of with the OTHER denominator (3 − i).
Rationalising each fraction separately, which doubles the work.

steps.label: Expand the numerator
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Expand both products, then collect the terms without i and the terms with i. The right side is i, which is 0 + 10i once multiplied by 10.

recall.must_convey: That the numerator expands to (3x + 3y − 6) + i(y − x), and the equation becomes that equal to 10i.
accept: expand to three x plus three y minus six plus i times y minus x and set it equal to ten i
the real part is three x plus three y minus six and the imaginary part is y minus x
multiply the ten across so the right side is ten i, the left is three x plus three y minus six plus i y minus x
expand cheste three x plus three y minus six plus i into y minus x, equals ten i
collect the real terms and the i terms after expanding both brackets

steps.why: Two complex numbers can only be compared part by part, so the left side has to be sorted into (real) + i(imaginary). Multiplying the 10 across first keeps the fractions out of the comparison.
common_mistakes: Sign slip in −xi + i or in yi − i, so the imaginary part comes out as x + y instead of y − x.
Forgetting to multiply the right side by 10.
Writing the right side as 10 instead of 10i.

steps.label: Compare parts
steps.margin_note: Third mark. The right side 10i has real part 0 and imaginary part 10. That gives one equation from each part.

recall.must_convey: That equating real parts gives x + y = 2 and equating imaginary parts gives y − x = 10.
accept: real parts give x plus y equals two and imaginary parts give y minus x equals ten
compare with zero plus ten i to get two equations x plus y two and y minus x ten
the real part is zero so x plus y is two, the imaginary part is ten so y minus x is ten
real parts compare cheste x plus y equals two, imaginary parts compare cheste y minus x equals ten
two simultaneous equations from the two parts

steps.why: Equality of complex numbers is two real equalities at once. Two unknowns, two equations — the question is designed so that this comparison is exactly enough to fix x and y.
common_mistakes: Setting the real part equal to 10 instead of 0.
Not dividing 3x + 3y − 6 = 0 by 3, which makes the next step messier.
Losing the sign in y − x = 10.

steps.label: Solve for x and y
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Adding (1) and (2) removes x at once. Then put y back into (1). Check: −4 + 6 = 2 and 6 − (−4) = 10.

recall.must_convey: That adding the two equations gives y = 6, and then x = −4.
accept: add the two equations to get two y equals twelve so y is six and then x is minus four
y equals six and x equals minus four
adding removes x, y is six, substitute back and x is minus four
rendu equations add cheste y six, x minus four vasthundi
solve the pair to get x minus four and y six

steps.why: The x terms in (1) and (2) have opposite signs, so adding is the quickest route. Both answers are real, as the question promised — a non-real x or y would signal an earlier slip.
common_mistakes: Subtracting instead of adding, which gives 2x = −8 and is also fine — but then y must come from (1), not be guessed.
Writing x = 4 by dropping the sign.
Not checking the pair in the original equation.
